To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the rate of formation and decay of lac-specific RNA are affected by the same regulatory mechanisms that affect the rate of formation or decay of bulk RNA.
the accumulation of lac-specific RNA is controlled by the same mechanisms that regulate the expression of the lac genes.

the rate of lac-specific mRNA synthesis in induced cells is linear for the first three minutes and then becomes constant, and that the rate of synthesis of mRNA complementary to the promoter-distal lac Y-A gene is slower than the rate of synthesis complementary to the promoter-proximal lac Z gene.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism whereby glucose inhibits transcription of the lac operons in Escherichia col.
the mechanism of regulation of the lac operons of E. coli.
the regulation of gene expression in the lac operon, a well-characterized operon of Escherechia coli.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
catabolite and transient repression act at the same site, i.e., the lac promoter site, and that the only effect is the inhibition of initiation of transcription.
the lac promoter region is a single site of transcription initiation and that the lac promoter is a site of transcription initiation which is sensitive to catabolite and transient repression.
the rate of lac-specific transcription increases linearly for the first few minutes after induction and then remains constant.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the initiation of RNA chain elongation is not affected by the catabolite or by transient repression, but the initiation of RNA transcription is inhibited.
the lac operon is transcribed as a single polycistronic message.
catabolite and transient repression inhibit the initiation of lac RNA synthesis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
lac-specific transcription begins before the lac Z gene is transcribed.
the lac operon is a good system for studying the regulation of transcription.

lac-specific RNA is synthesized at the lac promoter in a manner consistent with a model for the control of the lac operons that involves the binding of a cAMP-CRP complex at the lac promoter and the binding of a repressor protein to the lac O1 operator.
